question: On Wednesday 8 December 2023, the Danish Minister of Health stated that the Danish Ministry of Health had been in dialogue with the Commission regarding the interpretation of the EU Tobacco Products Directive, among other things, with the aim of investigating the labeling practices of products in other EU countries.1 I would like to request that the Commission provide details of the dialogue with the Danish Ministry of Health. 1.
Does the Commission still advocate the right to intellectual property and the freedom to conduct a business as protected by the EU Charter of Fundamental Rights?
Does the Commission agree that Member States should ensure that trade secrets and other confidential information are treated in a confidential manner?

Does the Commission agree that ingredients must be listed on packaging but that this can be done in a way that protects trade secrets, for instance by grouping flavourings comprising a very small volume as ‘flavourings’?
answer: The EU has a robust framework for the protection of intellectual property and trade secrets. When implementing Union law, Member States must take account of the Charter of Fundamental Rights. The Court has interpreted the Charter in cases concerning intellectual property rights including those referred to by the Honourable Member.

It is settled case law that the protection of business secrets is a general principle of law. (2) The Trade Secrets Directive (Directive (EU) 2016/943) (3) provides minimum standards against the unlawful acquisition, disclosure and use of trade secrets but Member States may provide for more protection. Account should be taken of the situations in which the directive is not applicable (for example Article 1(2)).

(4) Under the Tobacco Products Directive 2014/40/EU (TPD) (5), manufacturers and importers of tobacco and related products are required to submit to the competent authorities information necessary to carry out their regulatory tasks (6). It must be ensured that trade secrets and other confidential information are protected.

But it must also be ensured that the general public receives the greatest possible transparency of product information. The labelling of tobacco products shall not include elements or features specified in Article 13 of the TPD. This applies also for electronic cigarettes and refill containers with limited exceptions concerning information on the nicotine content and flavourings.

Unit packets and any outside packaging of electronic cigarettes and refill containers must include a leaflet and information as per Article 20(4) of the TPD, including a list of all ingredients contained in the product in descending order of the weight (7). That information is important to protect human health and safety.
